features.title: Browse aliases by scope and environment
features.summary: Search metadata-only aliases across all, project, global, and local scopes; choose projects through the shared picker, which opens on projects and lists confirmed secondary JJ workspaces on their own tab, and identify the current host-local scope.

configuration.constraints: One of all, project, global, or local.

failureModes: Duplicate alias and environment across scopes makes value operations unavailable.
A scope without a selected folder cannot claim project-specific results.
An unavailable or failing secret CLI shows only its load error, never an empty catalog.

externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Inject a fake CLI runner with synthetic alias metadata and values; never read a real vault or session credential.

features.title: Reveal on click and copy without revealing
features.summary: Hovering a masked value offers "Click to reveal"; a click reveals that one alias and environment through the Host, and it masks again after the configured timeout, on blur, Esc, scope change, refresh, or unmount. Copy goes through the Host CLI without revealing.

configuration.constraints: Integer from 0 to 60 seconds; zero keeps the notice persistent.
Boolean; clear revealed values when focus leaves the view.

failureModes: Secret values are never included in catalog metadata, argv, or notices.
Blur or navigation clears client plaintext before another reveal.

features.title: Add a secret inline under the list
features.summary: Add secret appends an editable row: an env-var style name and a masked value (or Generate on this Host from the row menu, which also offers Copy and Delete). Enter or leaving the row saves it to the viewed scope (the selected project under All) and the default environment; the split arrow opens the detailed dialog.
failureModes: A draft with no value is not saved: the Host refuses empty manual values, so the row asks for a value or Generate.
A name that already exists in the environment is flagged before any write.
A failed save keeps the draft and its value in the row and says so.

externalDependencies.boundary: secret set over stdin or with --generate through the managed secret executable.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Put the e2e fake secret CLI first on the Host PATH with a synthetic JSON store; never invoke a real vault.

features.title: Create, edit, rename, and remove aliases safely
features.summary: Add through a required-first dialog (alias, scope defaulting to the selected project, environment prod, generated or masked value, Advanced fold for item metadata), edit metadata/value, rename aliases, remove one alias without deleting the vault item, or explicitly delete the vault entry.
reach: click button "More ways to add a secret"
failureModes: Duplicate alias/environment collisions are blocked before writes.
Manual values travel through stdin and are not echoed in process output.

features.title: Create and bind from a secret-reference field
features.summary: A marked controlled input opens a compact masked create-and-bind form. The Secret Catalog Host stores the value, the consumer receives only a reference, and a duplicate alias can bind the existing record instead of failing creation.
failureModes: Invalid aliases, environments, and folderless project/local scopes are rejected before storage.
A failed bind retains only the stored reference for retry; the value is cleared and never sent to the consumer.
A duplicate alias offers to bind its unique existing record; ambiguous duplicates must be resolved in the catalog.

externalDependencies.boundary: Secret value writes and metadata reads.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Use the fake secret CLI with synthetic values; assert manual values travel on stdin and consumer fields receive references only.

verification.testName: validates alias, environment, and a non-empty bounded value through the shared schemas
keeps a stored reference for retry when binding fails, without creating a second secret

features.title: Repair a secret reference that does not resolve
features.summary: A configured secret:ALIAS[@env] that the Host cannot resolve names the reference and the typed reason (alias missing from every scope or only in a project, environment missing, several scopes, unreadable or empty vault value, secret CLI missing, locked or failing) and offers Set value in the right scope, Pick another secret, Open in Secret Catalog on that alias, and Re-check. It warns before a global write lands in a symlinked config.
failureModes: A reference that resolves shows no card; one that starts resolving after a repair says so once.
CLI failures offer no write: they name the cause (PATH, locked vault, doctor) and offer Re-check.
Ambiguous aliases are never guessed; the card opens the Catalog on that alias.
A Host without the status verb shows a check-failed card with Re-check instead of a blank one.

externalDependencies.boundary: Metadata reads, the value read that proves resolution, and value writes.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Use the fake secret CLI with synthetic values; no real vault is read.

verification.testName: maps CLI failures to their typed codes
says the alias is missing from every scope, or names the project that holds it
warns before a global write lands in a symlinked config, and only then

features.title: Set up a Jev key from chat
features.summary: The latest completed chat turn offers the compact masked setup form only when Jev is enabled, no key resolves, and no reference is already configured. A bound but unresolvable reference gets a repair warning instead of a duplicate-create form.

A configured but unresolvable reference shows the reference repair card, not another create form.
The raw key stays out of conversation content and Backlog settings; only its reference is bound.
Secret CLI or Settings failures show an error without putting the key in the chat.
